1 · Retention breakdown

curve100 samples, stored one per percent runtime18:31 gone by 0:3045.4% at halfway25% still watching methodhazard = (present before − present after) ÷ present before at each moment; baseline = mean hazard of the previous 5 moments, floored; flagged when the excess viewers lost beyond baseline ranks high; a rise is a rewind only when no comparable drop precedes it and the lift survives the next sample

2 · Each flagged moment: from curve to note

drop0:10
1 · what the curve showedThe opening 23 seconds shed nearly half the room, running almost twice the channel's usual intro loss (*17.50% stop rate, 1.9x channel norm, 4,330 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“this one isn't even really the perfect one” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The video opens with a greeting and a hedged tease — "i might be buying a van tomorrow" followed by admitting "this one isn't even really the perfect one" — undercutting the title's promise. 4 · how (the next move)Cut 0:10-0:38 and open on the 3:03 "it's a done deal" reveal, then flash back to the search. 5 · rationaleJoos: never restate the premise the thumbnail sold, and never open on a greeting — lead with the strong-emotion moment the audience is already rewinding to.
peak2:24
1 · what the curve showedAudience rose 9.5 points and held for thirteen samples, the longest sustained lift in the video (*+446 viewers regained, audience reaches 30.3%*). 2 · evidence at that second“road trip with me to california” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers are rewinding the road-trip plan reveal — "another month here until my sister can get two weeks off of work to take the road trip with me to california." 4 · how (the next move)Tease "California road trip with my sister" in the first 30 seconds as an unresolved stake for the video. 5 · rationaleJoos: keep the narrative suspense layer live across the whole video — a concrete future stake, teased early, holds the middle that currently sags to 25.4%.
peak2:36
1 · what the curve showedAudience rose 6.7 points and held for nine samples in the 67th percentile against similar videos (*+344 viewers regained, audience reaches 32.3%*). 2 · evidence at that second“very cool i think that's everything” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers replay the "very cool i think that's everything" beat that immediately precedes the purchase — the pre-reveal buildup itself is holding. 4 · how (the next move)Trial a 20-second riser under 2:32-3:03 to extend anticipation into the reveal, and A/B against the current cut. 5 · rationaleJoos: start anticipatory risers ~20 seconds before a key moment — retention flattens through the buildup, and this stretch already proves the audience wants more of it. cautionThe riser must not signal an outro or resolve the tension early — measure success by whether the 3:00-3:30 window holds above 33% audience.
peak2:47
1 · what the curve showedAudience climbed 8.7 points and held for six samples, sitting in the 71st percentile against similar videos (*+480 viewers regained, audience reaches 35.1%*). 2 · evidence at that second“it's a done deal it's a done deal” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers are rewinding to the "it's a done deal it's a done deal i can't believe it" moment — the actual purchase reveal the title promised. 4 · how (the next move)Front-load this exact line into the first 10 seconds as the cold open, then cut back to the search. 5 · rationaleJoos: a reveal that earns rewinds is an asset — tease it early and structure toward it, because the intro currently buries what the audience most wants.
drop3:09
1 · what the curve showedA 33-second stretch loses viewers at exactly the channel's usual rate for this position (*2.07% stop rate, 1.0x channel norm, 489 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“maybe we should go to walmart first” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The purchase beat resolves into a mundane errands segue — "maybe we should go to walmart first" for a "steering wheel cover" — releasing tension right after the reveal. 4 · how (the next move)Move the Walmart errand to a montage after 4:00 and cut straight from 3:09 into driving the van away. 5 · rationaleJoos: never place a flat beat right after a payoff — viewers feel released and leave; the reveal at 3:03 is the peak, protect it with continued momentum.
drop14:49
1 · what the curve showedA 33-second lull loses a fifth of the remaining room at nearly five times the channel's usual rate here (*7.20% stop rate, 13.3x spike, 892 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“it's so rare that i feel this good” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The creator stops the action to monologue about feelings — "i just want to say again how good i feel" and "it's so rare that i feel this good" — with no new information landing. 4 · how (the next move)Cut 14:39-15:22 entirely and rejoin on the next visible change inside the van. 5 · rationaleJoos: pacing is the flow of NEW information — something should visibly change every ~5 seconds, and repeated feelings-talk is exactly the repetition to kill.
